title: RDA ambassador
text:
This site is a starting point for connecting domain communities with the Research Data Alliance (RDA), FAIR data practices, and practical resources that support data sharing and reuse.
Explore Resources

title: RDA ambassador
text:
Why This Site Matters
RDA ambassadors help bridge the gap between the global RDA community and domain-specific research practice. They support awareness of RDA outputs, connect communities with relevant expertise, and help translate FAIR and open science approaches into disciplinary contexts.




Resource Discovery
Browse guides, tools, outputs, and training materials that can be adapted to your community.
View Library »






Community Connectors
Find ambassadors, understand their expertise, and identify who to contact for outreach or collaboration.
Meet Ambassadors »






Contribute
Add resources, suggest updates, and help strengthen links between RDA and your discipline.
Get Involved »

title: Updates & Changelog
text:
This document tracks all major updates, new features, and changes made to the RDA ambassador website project.





Initialized core Quarto website project structure.
Created _quarto.yml for global site configuration, search, and navigation.
Added custom styling via styles.scss for a modern, responsive design and micro-animations.
Scaffolded core pages: index.qmd (homepage with hero banner), about.qmd, ambassadors.qmd, resources.qmd, and contribute.qmd.
Created ARCHITECTURE.md to document the technical stack, styling methodology, and content workflows.
Created UPDATES.md to serve as a persistent changelog.
Reorganized project structure into /data, /pages, /assets, and /docs for better scalability.
Translated all project documentation and site scaffolding to English.

title: Get Involved & Contribute
text:
Current Working Method
For now, the simplest route is to manage updates through the repository and structured data files such as data/resources.csv and data/ambassadors.csv.
Found a typo or want to expand a section? You can also edit the .qmd pages directly. Quarto uses standard Markdown, which keeps the site easy to maintain.

title: FAQ
text: The Research Data Alliance (RDA) is a global, community-driven organisation that works to enable research data sharing and reuse across disciplines, technologies, and countries.

title: FAQ
text: The Research Data Alliance (RDA) is a global, community-driven organisation that works to enable research data sharing and reuse across disciplines, technologies, and countries.

title: FAQ
section: What is an RDA ambassador in the context of this site?
text:
What is an RDA ambassador in the context of this site?
An RDA ambassador, as presented here, is someone who helps connect a research community, discipline, or thematic area with relevant RDA practices, outputs, and collaboration opportunities.

title: FAQ
section: Is this website the official global RDA website?
text:
Is this website the official global RDA website?
No. The global RDA website is rd-alliance.org. This site should be understood as a supporting entry point connected to ambassador activity within the broader RDA ecosystem.

title: FAQ
section: What kind of resources can be published here?
text:
What kind of resources can be published here?
Guides, tutorials, videos, links, case studies, event information, and other materials that help communities engage with FAIR data and relevant RDA work.

title: FAQ
text:
Who should use this site?

Researchers and data practitioners
Community coordinators and trainers
People looking for domain-relevant FAIR and RDA materials
Contributors who want to share resources or updates

title: FAQ
text:
How can someone contribute?
They can contribute by proposing resources, updating ambassador profiles, sharing events, or suggesting improvements to the site structure and content.

title: About Us
text:
This website is designed as a starting point for an RDA ambassador initiative connected to the broader Research Data Alliance (RDA) ecosystem.
RDA is a global, community-driven organisation that works to enable the open sharing and reuse of research data across disciplines, technologies, and countries. Within that context, ambassadors can help translate RDA outputs, FAIR data practices, and open science approaches into the needs of specific communities.



Promote: Share FAIR data practices, open science approaches, and relevant RDA outputs.
Connect: Act as a bridge between domain communities and the wider RDA network.
Support: Provide orientation, resources, and practical pathways for adoption.





RDA provides the wider international community, working groups, interest groups, recommendations, and outputs.
This site can serve as a local, thematic, or programme-level entry point for ambassador activities.
Ambassadors can help communities discover where RDA is useful in day-to-day research data practice.





Presenting the purpose and scope of the ambassador initiative
Publishing ambassador profiles and areas of expertise
Curating resources for specific disciplines or use cases
Sharing updates, events, and community opportunities
Providing a simple route for contributions and collaboration

title: Project Architecture
text:
This repository contains the source code for the RDA ambassador website, built using Quarto. It is designed to be a modern, dynamic static site that centralizes resources and ambassador profiles for the Research Data Alliance community.



To keep the project organized as it grows and participants add more resources, we use a modular and scalable structure:



_quarto.yml: Main Quarto configuration (navigation, metadata, theme).
styles.scss: Custom styles (RDA colors, animations).
index.qmd, about.qmd: Main static pages.





docs/ARCHITECTURE.md: Technical project documentation (this file).
docs/UPDATES.md: History of changes and updates.




Instead of creating a page for each resource, we use simple databases: - data/ambassadors.csv: Information about the ambassadors. - data/resources.csv: Metadata for all resources (title, author, domain, file link).



To avoid cluttering the root with .qmd files: - pages/ambassadors/index.qmd: Ambassadors directory. - pages/resources/index.qmd: Main resource search engine. - pages/contribute/index.qmd: Contribution guide for users.



This is where physical files (PDFs, images) are stored, organized logically to avoid chaos: - assets/images/ambassadors/: Profile pictures. - assets/resources/domains/agriculture/: Domain-specific documents for agriculture. - assets/resources/domains/humanities/: Humanities documents. - assets/resources/shared/: General guides (e.g., FAIR data principles) that apply to everyone.
This strict separation between code (.qmd), data (.csv), and files (assets/) ensures the repository remains easy to maintain even with thousands of resources.




To make contributions seamless, the site will implement a data-driven architecture. Instead of hardcoding resources into Markdown, structured data (e.g., lists of resources or ambassadors) will be pulled from data files (like data/resources.csv or data/ambassadors.csv). During the Quarto build process, this data is rendered dynamically. This empowers non-technical contributors to update the site simply by editing a spreadsheet or CSV file.



The site leverages Quarto’s built-in Bootstrap 5 integration: 1. Base Theme: Starting with the cosmo theme for a clean, professional baseline. 2. Customizations: The styles.scss overrides Bootstrap default variables to introduce a bespoke primary/secondary color palette. 3. Components: Custom utility classes (.hero-banner, .resource-card) are used extensively to create premium layouts and subtle animations that enhance user experience.
